title: Manipulating Monomicelle Monolayer Assembly via Salt Effect Toward Tailorable Mesoporous Polydopamine Superstructures for Aqueous Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT The inherent thermodynamic instability of isotropic soft micelles drives their conventional bulk aggregation toward multilayered mesoporous structures, while stabilizing monomicelles and manipulating their monolayer assembly into mesoporous superstructures poses a significant challenge. Here, we report a salt effect‐modulated monomicelle assembly strategy for the precise construction of monolayer mesoporous polydopamine superstructures. The concerted salt effect arising from Debye screening and salting‐out stabilizes the composite monomicelles, reduces their hydrophilicity, and promotes their migration and lateral monolayer assembly at the emulsion interface. Increasing the salt content accelerates assembly kinetics, enhances interfacial affinity, and increases micellar rigidity, enabling tunable interfacial coverage and thereby producing a series of monolayer mesoporous superstructures, including monolayer honeycomb‐like mesoporous nanosheets, monolayer honeycomb‐like mesoporous vesicles, monolayer compound eye‐like mesoporous vesicles, and monolayer compound eye‐like mesoporous nanosheets. As a proof of concept, monolayer honeycomb‐like nanosheets with open mesochannels and abundant functional groups were demonstrated as a nano‐ion divider. By homogenizing the ion flux and enhancing ion affinity and transport, this architecture enables dendrite‐free Sn aqueous batteries with an exceptional lifespan of 2794 h. This work opens new avenues for constructing monolayer superstructures with unparalleled architectural modularization.

title: Electrochemically Directed Orientation in Two-Dimensional Conductive Metal-Organic Framework Thin Films
abstract: Controlling the preferred crystallographic orientation of two-dimensional (2D) conductive metal-organic framework (c-MOF) films is essential for maximizing anisotropic charge transport and unlocking their full potential in advanced applications. However, the factors governing film orientation during electrochemical growth on a substrate remain poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that the preferred orientation of amine-derived Ni3(HITP)2 films can be modulated by small changes in applied potential during anodic electrodeposition. Films deposited at 0.05 V exhibit smooth morphologies and pronounced (002) texture, consistent with preferential alignment of the layered framework parallel to the substrate. Increasing the potential to 0.10 V suppresses the dominant (002) contribution and increases the relative prominence of low-angle reflections associated with (100) family, indicating a shift in preferred orientation toward (100). Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy confirm that both films retain similar Ni-HITP framework chemistry and Ni coordination environments. Electrochemical measurements reveal distinct potential-dependent growth kinetics, with 0.05 V exhibiting slower, more gradual precursor activation and 0.10 V producing a larger, earlier current response consistent with more rapid generation of reactive species. Extension to catechol-derived Cu3(HHTP)2 reveals analogous potential-dependent changes in morphology, diffraction behavior, and electrochemical growth response. These findings establish applied potential as a practical parameter for modulating growth behavior and preferred crystallographic orientation in electrochemically deposited 2D c-MOF films.

title: Macrocycle 2D COF Single Crystal
abstract: Abstract We report the synthesis of a two-dimensional (2D) covalent organic framework (COF) single crystal, termed COF-900, constructed from a geminiarene-type macrocycle linker, biphenyl-extended pillar[3]arene containing nine phenyl units. The atomically accurate structure was resolved by three-dimensional electron diffraction (3D ED) of the 2D COF single crystal with a resolution of 1.2 Å, unveiling the conformation of the macrocycle in the layered backbone as well as AB interlayer stacking. The macrocycle exhibits a similar stacking mode in both the COF and the molecular crystal of the linker, suggesting prealignment of linkers during COF crystal growth through a mechanism termed alignment-led framework assembly (ALFA). Cryo-transmission electron microscopy images further provided direct real-space visualization of the macrocycle, where three types of interconnected pores were clearly visualized with sizes of 1.1, 1.5, and 2.3 nm.

title: Orthogonal Self‐Assembled Two‐Dimensional Charge‐Transfer Cocrystals With Superior Photothermal Stability for Low‐Loss NIR‐II Waveguiding and Epitaxial Heterostructure Fabrication
abstract: ABSTRACT Low‐dimensional organic near‐infrared (NIR) crystals hold tremendous potential for integrated photonics. However, simultaneously achieving two‐dimensional (2D) structural growth and low‐loss waveguiding within the NIR‐II region remains a formidable challenge due to one‐dimensional (1D) packing tendencies imposed by strong charge transfer (CT) interactions. In this study, we strategically choose the extended π‐conjugated structure donor dithieno[2,3‐d:2',3'‐d']benzo[1,2‐b:4,5‐b']dithiophene and the strong electron‐withdrawing acceptor tetracyanoquinodimethane, and report the first large‐scale preparation of 2D organic CT cocrystal microsheets with NIR‐II emission at 1050 nm via a gas‐phase self‐assembly. The strategically expanded conjugation framework not only further promotes the luminescence red‐shift but also introduces an interaction network with orthogonal directions, counterbalancing the intrinsic 1D stacking constraints brought by the strong CT interactions and guiding the crystals into a thermodynamically stable 2D morphology. The compact network plays a crucial role in endowing the material with exceptional structural and photothermal stability, as well as low‐loss optical waveguiding. Furthermore, attributed to the extremely low lattice‐mismatch rate, 1D‐2D branched heterostructures were constructed, which demonstrated efficient energy transfer (ET) and cross‐band optical signal conversion over 600 nm. This work breaks new ground in extending 2D organic cocrystals into the NIR‐II region and provides a promising material platform for low‐loss, and integrated NIR optoelectronic devices.

title: Flexible 2D Donor‐Acceptor MOFs Enable Tunable and Pressure‐Responsive TSCT–TADF for Heterocrystal Photonic Logic
abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) materials that combine high efficiency, color tunability, and dynamic stimulus responsiveness are highly desirable for adaptive photonic technologies, yet remain difficult to realize within a single crystalline platform. Here, flexible two‐dimensional (2D) donor‐acceptor (D–A) metal‐organic frameworks (MOFs) are developed through integrating an aggregation‐induced‐emission‐active triphenylamine donor with size‐matched electron‐deficient acceptors. Solvent‐directed assembly, donor conformational flexibility, and acceptor electronic modulation cooperatively regulate the D–A packing and through‐space charge‐transfer (TSCT) effect. The resulting MOFs exhibit broadly tunable TADF emission (474–635 nm), delayed lifetimes (0.11–7.65 µs), and photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQY, 0.52%–74.24%). Relative to the DMF‐derived structures, the DMA‐derived MOFs display increases of up to 51‐fold in delayed lifetime and 6‐fold in PLQY, while calculations support an unconventional high‐lying reverse intersystem crossing (hRISC) pathway. More importantly, the structural adaptability of the layered frameworks enables pressure‐induced reconfiguration of D–A interactions, giving rise to reversible piezochromic TSCT–TADF with emission shifts of up to 113 nm. A multicomponent heterocrystal is further constructed to translate pressure‐dependent emission changes into optical logic operations. These results establish flexible 2D D–A MOFs as a dynamic platform for integrating efficient TADF, mechanical responsiveness, and heterocrystal photonic functionality.

title: Reactive Phase Conversion‐Enabled 1D/3D Heterostructure Engineering Toward High‐Performance Perovskite Photovoltaics
abstract: ABSTRACT We report a reactive phase conversion strategy for 1D/3D heterostructure engineering in perovskite photovoltaics. During crystallization, 1‐carboxymethyl‐3‐methylimidazolium chloride (CMMIMCl) reacts with PbI 2 , enabling the in situ formation of one‐dimensional (1D) CMMIMPbI 3 within the 3D perovskite matrix. This precursor‐level process simultaneously consumes residual PbI 2 and constructs an internally coupled 1D/3D heterostructure, which regulates crystallization kinetics, promotes oriented crystal growth, and redistributes residual stress. The resulting 1D framework further modulates defect energetics and interfacial charge transport, thereby suppressing non‐radiative recombination and ion migration. Notably, at an optimized low CMMIMCl concentration, the initially formed 1D‐related species potentially serve as crystallization templates, modifying the crystallization pathway and facilitating more complete conversion of PbI 2 into high‐quality 3D perovskite. Benefiting from these integrated structural and optoelectronic improvements, inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs) achieve a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 27.09% (certified 26.98%), while scalable perovskite modules reach 22.01%. Furthermore, wide‐bandgap PSCs achieve a PCE of 23.66%, enabling perovskite/tunnel oxide passivated contact tandem devices with an efficiency of 33.03% (certified 32.98%). This work establishes a versatile route for simultaneous regulation of crystallization, defects, strain, and charge transport in high‐performance perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Multiscale Modeling of Virus Capsid Self-Assembly Reveals How Small Molecule Antivirals Can Redirect Assembly Pathways and Products
abstract: Abstract Controlling the assembly of a virus capsid, a regular complex of hundreds of subunits, has applications for development of antivirals and for development of nanocontainers. Recent work has shown that a class of small molecules called capsid assembly modulators (CAMs) is promising for treating Hepatitis B virus (HBV). CAMs bind to HBV capsid proteins and alter their self-assembly, leading to nonfunctional and malformed structures. The mechanisms by which CAMs alter capsid assembly remain unclear. Here, we use a kinetic Monte Carlo (KMC) model for HBV capsid assembly to simulate how CAMs affect this complex reaction. The model is parametrized from all-atom simulations, resulting in unprecedented correlation between simulation and biochemical and structural observations. Simulations reproduce the effect of CAMs on experimental assembly products and their distributions. By analyzing assembly trajectories, we clarify the roles of thermodynamics and kinetics in determining assembly products, identify assembly mechanisms, and predict the key intermediates that lead to either capsids or malformed structures. Our findings enhance our fundamental understanding of capsid assembly, help advance the development of CAMs as a treatment for HBV and, more broadly, inform efforts to direct self-assembly pathways toward specific products.

title: Precursor–Cavity Compatibility Directs C−N Bond Evolution Toward Edge Reconstruction for H 2 O 2 Electrosynthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT ZIF‐derived metal–nitrogen–carbon (M−N−C) catalysts provide a versatile platform for constructing atomically dispersed metal sites, yet their pyrolysis‐driven local coordination evolution remains largely governed by stochastic reconstruction processes. The lack of predictive structural descriptors linking molecular precursors with atomic‐scale active‐site evolution limits the rational design of high‐performance M−N−C catalysts. Here, we identify precursor–cavity compatibility as a key geometric descriptor that steers confined pyrolysis pathways and regulates C−N bond cleavage, leading to the formation of defect‐rich, edge‐reconstructed Co−N 4 environments. The optimized Co(bpy) 3 ‐NC achieves 95.9% H 2 O 2 selectivity at 0.60 V versus RHE and sustains nearly 90% Faradaic efficiency for 120 h at 200 mA cm −2 in an ambient‐air‐fed flow cell. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the reconstructed Co−N 4 environments optimize Co−OOH interaction by balancing *OOH stabilization with O−O bond preservation, thereby favoring the selective 2e − ORR pathway. Furthermore, the electrogenerated dilute H 2 O 2 stream enables effective nitrite regulation in recirculating aquaculture systems, demonstrating the potential of integrating molecularly guided catalyst design with decentralized chemical production. This work establishes precursor–cavity compatibility as a rational design principle for steering atomic‐scale coordination evolution in confined pyrolysis.

title: Anodic Selective Etching: A Mechanism‐Centric Perspective for Electrochemical Subtractive Manufacturing
abstract: ABSTRACT Anodic selective etching (ASE) is a precision electrochemical subtractive manufacturing strategy that enables controllable material removal, interfacial reconstruction, and morphology evolution under electrochemically controlled conditions. Unlike material‐centric reviews that mainly catalogue substrates or products, this mechanism‐centric framework reveals common electrochemical principles, enabling cross‐material comparison, transferable design rules, and predictive control over selectivity, reaction location, and structural evolution. This review unifies ASE across material platforms and structural scales through five dominant modes: composition‐ and phase‐selective anodic dissolution, structural site‐selective anodic etching, semiconductor carrier‐ and space‐charge‐controlled etching, film‐ and passivation‐controlled subtraction, and geometry‐ or three‐phase boundary‐localized etching, together with representative coupled mechanisms. The roles of anodic material characteristics, electrolyte composition, and electrochemical parameters in defining selectivity windows, localization behavior, and structural outcomes are critically discussed. These mechanisms enable low‐dimensional materials, porous and core–shell architectures, surface finishing and shaping, and meniscus‐localized tip fabrication. Key challenges in multicomponent selectivity, electrolyte sustainability, and scalable manufacturing are outlined, alongside opportunities in in situ and operando characterization, multi‐physics modeling, and data‐driven optimization toward reproducible and programmable electrochemical manufacturing.

title: Ultrarobust and Thermo‐Mechano‐Photo‐Responsive Elastomers by Supramolecular and Dynamic 3D Topological Architectures
abstract: ABSTRACT Mechanically robust elastomers are being widely used in multi‐stimuli‐responsive systems including closed‐loop recycling, information encryption, and advanced photolithography. However, their advancement is hindered by an inherent trade‐off: structural integrity for mechanical robustness versus molecular‐level reversibility for stimuli responsiveness. In this study, we constructed ultrarobust recyclable and photo‐responsive supramolecular‐dynamic covalent networks (SDCN) based on molecular engineering of anthracene‐functionalized poly(urethane‐urea‐amide) (PUUA) networks with hindered urea motifs. Well‐designed SDCN achieves multiscale assembly through coordinated π–π stacking, hydrogen bonding, and dynamic covalent interactions, creating dynamic coupling between soft‐chain crosslinks and self‐assembly hard domains, and driving microphase separation. Under stretching, strain‐activated disassembly of dynamically assembled nanostructures synergizes with stress‐induced crystallization, in situ evolving three‐dimensional topological architectures and promoting strength‐toughness enhancement. Consequently, PUUA elastomers exhibit remarkable mechanical performance (100.17 MPa tensile strength, 1286.79% elongation and 498.15 MJ m −3 toughness at room temperature; 113.67 MPa strength and 667.8% elongation at −40°C) and recycling performance (92.4% recyclability via solvent reprocessing). Significantly, UV‐responsive anthracene photonic moieties combined with temperature‐mediated interfacial SDCN transition enable fluorescent encryption and sub‐micron photolithographic patterning. Therefore, this work coordinates dynamic thermal‐mechanical‐optical responses and multi‐scale molecular transition mechanisms, which can be expected to boost high‐precision photolithographic patterning and flexible microcircuit printing fields.

title: Supramolecular Assembly Amplifies the Optoelectronic Performance of Terpyridine-Based Transition Metallomesogens
abstract: Abstract By introducing a supramolecular strategy centered on a novel dendritic ruthenium(II) metallomesogen (Ru-M) functionalized with terpyridine ligands, it is demonstrated that guiding molecular-level hierarchical organization amplifies the electrochromic (EC) performance. Comprehensive structural analyses confirm that Ru-M spontaneously self-assembles into a well-defined and uniaxially oriented lamellar nanostructure. This molecular-level ordering creates highly efficient charge transport pathways, leading to substantially enhanced electrochromic performance compared with the disordered nonmesogenic chromogen (Ru-2Tpy). The organized assembly exhibits remarkable coloration efficiency, a low operating voltage, and superior cycling stability, achieving high optoelectronic efficiency even at a 7-fold lower ruthenium loading per unit area. This strategy of directed supramolecular organization highlights the critical role of nanostructural engineering in overcoming performance trade-offs in electrochromic systems, establishing that tailored supramolecular architectures provide a robust platform for maximizing optoelectronic functionality.

title: Mesoporous Defect-Assisted Ce-Doped Cu-SSZ-13 Enabling Low-Temperature NH3–SCR via Enhanced Oxygen Transfer
abstract: Abstract Coupling efficient redox cycling with molecular diffusion in confined microporous environments remains a central challenge in zeolite catalysis. In Cu-exchanged SSZ-13 catalysts for NH3-assisted NOx reduction, low-temperature activity is limited by sluggish Cu redox interconversion and mass-transport constraints, while incorporation of secondary cations often intensifies pore-diffusion penalties. Herein, we show that defect-mediated mesostructuring enables the stable incorporation of atomically dispersed Ce species within Cu-SSZ-13, forming a Cu–Ce adjacent structure that synergistically modulates transport and redox chemistry. In situ spectroscopic and isotope-labeling analyses combined with multiscale simulations reveal that the engineered defect network enhances NOx and NH3 diffusion, while Ce species anchored at defect-edge sites promote oxygen activation and accelerate Cu-NO2 intermediate formation. These effects collectively facilitate more efficient Cu2+/Cu+ cycling across a substantially broadened temperature window. The resulting catalyst achieves ≥90% NOx conversion between 147 and 560 °C. More broadly, this work establishes defect-enabled secondary-cation stabilization as a promising strategy to decouple diffusion limitations from redox optimization in confined catalytic systems.

title: Reaction‐Induced Dynamic Covalent Networking Enables Adaptive Vesicles and Hierarchical Biointerfaces
abstract: ABSTRACT Conventional vesicular assemblies often face challenges in balancing mechanical robustness with structural adaptability. Here, we develop a reaction‐induced dynamic covalent networking (RIDCN) strategy that integrates vesicle construction with adaptive biointerface engineering. Through the formation of interconnected imine and boronate ester linkages, RIDCN directs the assembly of non‐amphiphilic building blocks into vesicular structures, with dynamic covalent networks serving as integral membrane frameworks. This structural integration reinforces vesicle mechanics while preserving adaptive reorganization through reversible bond exchange. Beyond individual vesicles, RIDCN enables interfacial assembly on diverse implant substrates, forming adaptive coatings with antibacterial, antioxidant, immunomodulatory, and osteogenic activities. These findings demonstrate the potential of RIDCN to connect vesicle construction, mechanical adaptation, and multifunctional biointerface engineering within a unified material design strategy.

title: Deferoxamine‐Engineered Mesoporous Silica Nanoparticles Unlock High‐Valence Metal Channels for Multiplexed Mass Cytometry
abstract: ABSTRACT Mass cytometry (MC) enables highly multiplexed single‐cell protein analysis, but its full analytical potential remains constrained by the limited range of available mass tags. Here, we report deferoxamine‐engineered mesoporous silica nanoparticles (DFO‐MSNs) for high‐capacity loading of multiple underutilized high‐valent metal ions within a common nanoparticle scaffold. DFO‐MSNs accommodated Zr 4+ , Hf 4+ , Nb 5+ , and Ta 5+ at approximately 10 4 metal atoms per nanoparticle, with high metal retention in physiological buffers. Following PEGylation and antibody (Ab) conjugation, the resulting Zr‐, Nb‐, Hf‐, and Ta‐based probes enabled antigen‐specific detection of human peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) by co‐staining with commercial Maxpar reagents. Nb‐, Hf‐, and Ta‐loaded MSN_CD8a probes resolved CD8a+ cytotoxic T lymphocytes at titers as low as 30 NPs/cell. In a 30‐plex staining panel, Ta@MSN_CD25 resolved low‐abundance CD25 hi CD127 lo T reg ‐like cells with apparent population recovery comparable to the corresponding Maxpar reagent, while consuming ca. 35‐fold less Ab. Together, these results establish a modular strategy for incorporating underutilized high‐valent metals into functional mass tags and demonstrate the feasibility of integrating MSN‐based probes into multiplexed MC immunophenotyping workflows.

title: Quaternary carbon–guided carbocation cascade rearrangement to enantioenriched polycycles
abstract: Polycyclic frameworks are prevalent in natural products and bioactive molecules, yet their efficient enantioselective synthesis remains a longstanding challenge. Carbocation cascade cyclization is a textbook reaction that has transformed the synthesis of fused polycycles, but extending this strategy to bridged architectures requires precise control over highly reactive carbocation intermediates while overcoming the intrinsic energetic barrier of transannular cyclization. Herein, we report a quaternary-carbon-guided carbocation cascade rearrangement platform that enables enantioselective and divergent assembly of complex polycyclic architectures from readily available substrates. An enantioenriched quaternary center, installed via transition-metal-catalyzed allylation, serves as a temporary structural linchpin in an acid-triggered cationic cascade rearrangement process, forming multiple bonds and chiral centers in a single step. In combination with pre-embedded quaternary centers, this strategy provides bicyclic and bridged polycyclic frameworks bearing multiple stereocenters with high enantioselectivity.

title: Balancing redox-mediated cytotoxicity and catalysis in natural product biosynthesis
abstract: Redox-mediated chemistry is central to both the biosynthesis and cytotoxicity of many natural products, yet how microbes balance these processes remains poorly understood. Here, we uncover a conserved mechanism that coordinates three redox-mediated processes in secondary metabolite biosynthesis: self-protection, prevention of substrate degradation, and late-stage biosynthesis. Using the antitumor antibiotic doxorubicin as a model system, we show that the vicinal oxygen chelate (VOC) protein DnrV prevents reactive oxygen species formation and substrate degradation while promoting P450 catalysis. We expand this paradigm to a conserved family of VOC-fold proteins, redox-associated cytotoxin-binding proteins (REACT), found across bacteria, fungi, and plants. REACT represents a multifunctional protein class that balances antibiotic assembly, self-protection, and prevention of metabolite destruction, providing a foundational understanding of production of redox-active natural products.

title: Nanoarchitectonics-Enabled Multifunctional Hydrogel with Artesunate-Loaded Mesoporous Silica Nanoparticles for Accelerated Diabetic Wound Healing via JAK1/STAT3-Mediated Macrophage Reprogramming
abstract: Abstract Diabetic wound healing is critically hindered by persistent macrophage dysfunction, characterized by an inability to transition from the pro-inflammatory M1 to the pro-healing M2 phenotype. Artesunate (ART) holds therapeutic promise for immunomodulation, yet its clinical translation is constrained by poor aqueous solubility and lack of sustained local delivery. Inspired by the concept of nanoarchitectonics, a post-nanotechnology paradigm that constructs functional material systems through the deliberate orchestration of atoms, molecules, and nanomaterials, we herein architect a multifunctional composite hydrogel (TA/CMCS/OSA/MSN@ART) via an integrated multi-step assembly strategy. This nanoarchitectonic design hierarchically integrates molecular building blocks, carboxymethyl chitosan, oxidized sodium alginate, and tannic acid, through Schiff-base dynamic covalent crosslinking and supramolecular hydrogen bonding, while simultaneously embedding ART-loaded mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSN@ART) as functional nanoscale units within the porous scaffold. This hydrogel demonstrates favorable physicochemical characteristics and exhibits notable biological properties, including low hemolysis, potent antibacterial and antioxidant activities, and high biocompatibility. Importantly, the ART-loaded hydrogel significantly accelerates diabetic wound healing by facilitating macrophage polarization toward the M2 phenotype. This effect appears to be closely associated with the activation of the JAK1/STAT3 signaling pathway. These findings establish nanoarchitectonics as a powerful and versatile methodology for designing advanced biomaterials, offering a transformative strategy for the management of chronic diabetic wounds.

title: Atomic Layer Ordering of 2D van der Waals Ion Channels Enables Ultrathin and Highly Selective Membranes
abstract: Abstract Developing ultrathin, highly selective membranes that emulate biological ion channels is a primary goal of synthetic membrane technology. Although two-dimensional (2D) materials offer a promising platform for constructing subnanometer fluidic channels, simultaneously achieving high permeance and excellent selectivity in 2D ionic membranes remains a significant challenge. This bottleneck originates from the complexities involved in controlling the precise structural arrangement within nanosheet assemblies. In this work, we demonstrate that the atomic-layer ordering of 2D van der Waals (vdW) ion channels is a decisive factor in achieving ultrathin, highly selective membranes. By assembling 2D titania nanosheets with atomic layer-by-layer regularity, we fabricate atomic stacking membranes (ASMs) that achieve near-unity ion selectivity within an ultrathin (∼50 nm) framework. The structural regularity of these ASMs causes continuous overlap of the electrical double layer throughout the 2D ion channels, facilitating robust electrostatic regulation and maximizing selectivity. The result is further confirmed by transmission electron microscopy, grazing-incidence wide-angle X-ray scattering analysis, and molecular dynamics simulations. Leveraging the “Lego-like” modular assembly advantage of ASMs, we demonstrate multifunctional heterostructural iontronic devices and gate-controlled iontronic transistors featuring on/off ratios up to 104. Furthermore, the well-ordered 2D ion channels within these ASMs enable high-performance osmotic energy harvesting. This solution-processable atomic-layer van der Waals assembly strategy for ultrathin and highly selective ASMs establishes a versatile platform for uniformly regulating 2D angstrom-scale ion transport, paving the way for advanced biomimetic iontronics and efficient energy conversion.

title: Molecular Origins of Lithium-Ion Transport in the Anionic Metal–Organic Framework SU-102
abstract: Abstract Metal–organic framework (MOF) quasi-solid electrolytes offer chemically tunable environments for ion transport, but the molecular roles of framework coordination and confined solvent remain unclear. We combined solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (ssNMR) measurements with molecular dynamics simulations to determine the Li+ transport mechanism in propylene carbonate (PC)-filled SU-102. Variable-temperature direct- and cross-polarization 7Li ssNMR reveal two distinct Li+ populations with different local tumbling dynamics. Our simulations identified Zr-associated, linker-associated, and fully PC-solvated Li+ coordination environments. The most strongly stabilizing Li+ site is not necessarily the one that carries transport: Zr-associated sites bind Li+ most strongly but form a discontinuous network along the pore axis, whereas the weaker-binding linker sites form a continuous one. Linker-associated Li+ also shows faster site-persistence decay and the largest trial-weighted displacement, and linker-to-linker hopping is the most frequent classified event, followed by Zr-to-Zr hopping. Chemical color-diffusion nonequilibrium molecular dynamics yielded an ionic conductivity of 1.34 ± 0.48 mS cm–1 along the one-dimensional channels and negligible conductivity perpendicular to them, giving an orientational average of 0.45 ± 0.16 mS cm–1, in close agreement with experiment (0.52 mS cm–1). Together, our results indicate that PC-assisted hopping between linker sites contributes more strongly than vehicular diffusion of fully solvated ions, with confined PC retained in the coordination shell across these transfers. These findings identify the balance between ion–framework stabilization and facile site-to-site exchange as a key design principle for reticular quasi-solid electrolytes.

title: A Three-Motif-Based One-Dimensional Covalent Organic Framework as an Efficient Cathode Material for Stable Rechargeable Sodium-Ion Batteries
abstract: Abstract Crystalline one-dimensional covalent organic frameworks (1D COFs) hold great promise for diverse applications; however, their synthesis remains challenging, as it requires simultaneous control over chain dimensionality and crystallization of polymeric chains that are intrinsically prone to entanglement. Here, we show that benzo[1,2-b:4,5-b′]difuran-2,6(3H,7H)-dione (BDFO), in the presence of isoquinoline, effectively compels the trifunctional monomer 2,4,6-tris(4-formylphenyl)-1,3,5-triazine (TPFT) to polymerize as a V-shaped ditopic linker, affording 1D zigzag chains that stack in a staggered arrangement to form the crystalline porous framework (CityU-31). CityU-31 exhibits a rectangular nanowire morphology with well-defined lattice fringes, a narrow pore-size distribution of 1–2 nm, and a surface area of 185 m2 g–1. Importantly, the V-shaped connectivity leaves one formyl group at each TPFT unit unreacted, and these pendant aldehydes serve as built-in handles for postsynthetic functionalization. As a proof of concept, a third motif was covalently linked via Knoevenagel condensation, converting the aldehyde groups into cyano functionalities to yield CityU-31-CN. Endowed with the cyano-decorated 1D backbone, CityU-31-CN delivers an extended voltage window (0.8–3.5 V), a high capacity of 160 mAh g–1 at 0.1 A g–1, and outstanding cycling stability (&gt;10,000 cycles). The intrinsic backbone reactivity of CityU-31 thus offers a versatile platform for postsynthetic modification, greatly expanding the application scope of crystalline 1D polymers.

title: An Autonomous Off-Grid MOF Water Harvester for Extreme Arabian Desert Conditions
abstract: Abstract Here we report an off-grid, passively heated, sorbent-assisted atmospheric water harvesting device. A metal–organic framework, Al(μ2–OH)[(E)-5-(2-carboxyvinyl)furan-2-carboxylate], is integrated as thin coatings in a disc-stack architecture to enhance moisture transport and heat transfer. Under laboratory conditions, the device harvested 660 mL kgMOF–1 day–1 and recovered 175 mL of water across two cycles in an 11.5 h simulated day, demonstrating multicyclic operation in a passively heated water harvester. Field tests near Al-Muzahmiyya (24.3416° N, 46.0203° E) in the Arabian Desert of Saudi Arabia, performed under frequent sandstorms and extremely challenging conditions for water harvesting (RHavg = 12.4%, Tavg = 20.5 °C), including dust-attenuated solar irradiance (Iavg = 496 W m–2) produced 46.7 ± 1.5 mL day–1 (185 mL kgMOF–1 day–1). title: High-Throughput Screening of Photocatalytic Metal–Organic Frameworks for CO2 Reduction Using Relational Data Extraction and Hierarchical Machine Learning
abstract: Abstract Photocatalytic carbon dioxide reduction (CO2RR) over metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) is governed by both framework features and reaction conditions, which complicate catalyst discovery and render general design rules difficult to establish. In this study, we develop a synergistic machine-learning workflow to integrate literature data extraction, electronic-property prediction, and hierarchical classification for prioritizing MOF photocatalysts. First, a literature-derived record-level data set containing catalyst compositions, structural descriptors, reaction conditions, and catalytic outcomes was curated through large language model (LLM)-assisted relation extraction followed by manual verification. Then, a transfer-learning crystal graph convolutional neural network (CGCNN) model was trained for band gap prediction at the Heyd-Scuseria-Ernzerhof screened hybrid functional (HSE06) level, achieving a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.31 eV against reference HSE06 calculations. Subsequently, a physically constrained multitask framework was employed to predict electron affinity (EA) and ionization potential (IP) for thermodynamic prescreening. Three record-level classifiers were constructed for activity screening (C1), performance classification (C2), and product selectivity prediction (C3). When applied to the Computation-Ready, Experimental (CoRE) MOF database under standardized gas- and liquid-phase inference settings, the workflow prioritized 639 primary candidates, with most assigned to CO formation. Probability calibration and applicability-domain analysis further identified 166 of these candidates (25.98%) as a more stringent calibrated, in-domain subset. Overall, this study provides a practical data-driven workflow for condition-resolved prioritization of MOF photocatalysts and analysis of descriptor-level trends associated with photocatalytic CO2RR.

title: From Empirical Tuning to Predictive Design: Decoupling Dynamic Bottlenecks in Photocatalytic H 2 O 2 Production via Z‐Score Importance Analysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Deconvoluting the intertwined dynamic bottlenecks of photogenerated charge and reaction substrates remains a fundamental bottleneck in heterogeneous photocatalysis due to the lack of reasonable and effective tools. This study presents a quantitative, interpretable framework to deconvolve the entangled factors limiting solar‐driven photocatalysis. Using Au(I)‐based covalent metal‐organic framework (CMOF‐Au) isomers with controlled stacking (AA, AB, and ABC) as a model platform for hydrogen peroxide photosynthesis, we applied a Z‑score and LOFO (Leave‐One‐Feature‐Out) importance analysis. This approach revealed that the dominant rate‐determining factor shifts with stacking: bulk charge transfer governs performance in AA stacking, whereas surface adsorption limits AB and ABC stacking. The method successfully quantifies the relative contribution weights of key functions (charge dynamics, interfacial transfer, surface adsorption, and mass transport) and demonstrates high predictive power across diverse photocatalysts, including covalent organic frameworks, porous aromatic frameworks, C 3 N 4 , and overall water‐splitting systems. By uncovering counterintuitive mechanisms, such as Simpson's paradox, our work establishes a generalizable strategy for decoupling multivariate factors, moving photocatalyst design from empirical tuning toward a predictive, function‐aware paradigm.

title: Engineering Stable and Targeted NIR/SWIR Imaging Agents through Metal-Organic Framework Nanoconfinement
abstract: Near-infrared (NIR) and shortwave infrared (SWIR) fluorophores offer significant potential for biomedical imaging owing to their deep tissue penetration and low background autofluorescence. However, their widespread application remains limited by poor aqueous solubility, aggregation-induced fluorescence loss, and inadequate stability in physiological environments. Here, we present a general nanoconfinement strategy that converts hydrophobic molecular fluorophores into stable, bright, and engineerable imaging nanocomposites through encapsulation within the large-pore metal-organic framework ZIF-71. Using IR-780 as a model dye and extending the approach to the larger fluorophores IR-813 and IR-1048, we demonstrate that in situ encapsulation preserves a predominantly monomeric dye population within the ZIF-71 framework, effectively suppressing aggregation across diverse aqueous environments, including physiologically relevant and high-salinity conditions. Compared with free dyes and benchmark micellar formulations, the IR-780@ZIF composites exhibit markedly improved resistance to aggregation, enhanced solution and photostability, and substantially increased fluorescence quantum yields and imaging brightness in water and phosphate-buffered saline. The benefits of confinement become increasingly pronounced for larger and more hydrophobic fluorophores, turning essentially dark free dyes IR-813 and IR-1048 in aqueous media into bright composites. Importantly, the external surface of the ZIF particles can be modified orthogonally through post-synthetic functionalization without compromising the optical properties of the encapsulated fluorophore. Surface incorporation of biotin and cell-penetrating peptide ligands enables tailored cellular delivery of the fluorophores, demonstrating the modularity of the platform. Collectively, these results establish large-pore ZIFs as versatile hosts for molecular NIR/SWIR fluorophores and highlight MOF nanoconfinement as a powerful strategy for integrating high-performance photophysics with customizable biological functionality for advanced imaging applications.

title: Superneutrality with Brush Layers for Directed Self-Assembly of High-χ Block Copolymers
abstract: Abstract Directed self-assembly (DSA) of block copolymers (BCPs) is promising for next-generation lithography, where achieving long-range ordering of out-of-plane lamellae is essential. This structure relies on neutral interactions at the substrate; however, surface tension disparities between blocks, notably in high-χ BCPs, make achieving neutral interfaces increasingly challenging. We demonstrate that brush immersion, i.e., the interpenetration of a grafted polymer layer into BCP domain interfaces, provides a robust pathway to a superneutrality state. Using graphoepitaxy of high-χ poly(1,1-dimethylsilacyclobutane)-block-polystyrene (PDMSB-b-PS) with a 9 nm half-pitch, we employ the ladder morphology (out-of-plane lamellae perpendicular to the sidewalls) as a sensitive energetic probe to validate this effect. Our results confirm a superneutral brush state, supported by a free energy model. Furthermore, we use grafted brushes with an optimal grafting density to maximize the brush interpenetration effect. This work establishes a framework for surface control in sub-10 nm BCP lithography.

title: 1,8-Azulenedicarboxylic Imides: Excited-State Properties and Catalytic Activity of a Nonalternant π-System
abstract: Abstract Imide-functionalized polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) represent an important class of π-conjugated molecules; however, their nonalternant isomers remain largely unexplored. Herein, we report the synthesis and investigation of the structural, photophysical, and excited-state properties of 1,8-azulenedicarboxylic imides as nonalternant isomers of 1,8-naphthalimides. These compounds retain the characteristic photophysics of the azulene framework, including near-infrared (NIR) absorption and anti-Kasha emission, while substitution at the imide nitrogen enables modulation of their excited-state electronic structures. QD-NEVPT2 calculations identified an S2–T1 pair with relatively large SOC and LE-to-CT character, suggesting a plausible ISC pathway associated with the observed singlet-oxygen photosensitization. Consequently, 1,8-azulenedicarboxylic imides function as an effective visible-light photocatalyst for the α-cyanation of secondary and tertiary amines. These findings demonstrate that the present nonalternant molecular design provides a strategy for tuning excited-state properties by modulating locally excited and charge-transfer states in imide chromophores.

title: Awakening Latent Diradicals to Enhance Antiferromagnetic Coupling between Localized Organic Spin Centers
abstract: Abstract Connecting persistent radicals through π-conjugated linkers provides a promising route for developing organic magnetic systems. However, the simultaneous realization of localized addressable spins and thermally robust antiferromagnetic (AFM) coupling remains challenging. Conventional approaches based on quinoidal versus aromatic resonance forms impose electronic constraints that limit access to this regime. Here, we introduce a molecular design principle in which the latent open-shell character of selected heterocyclic linkers is activated to significantly strengthen AFM interactions between localized radical centers. First-principles calculations reveal that this enhancement: i) originates from increased linker spin polarization acting synergistically with partial quinoidalization, and ii) is robust across a series of diradicals combining an expandable family of linkers with representative persistent radicals. We identify diradicals displaying pronounced open-shell character with unusually large singlet–triplet energy gaps typically associated with closed-shell systems. Extending this concept to two-dimensional covalent organic frameworks, we further show that our approach translates from discrete molecules to strongly AFM materials.

title: Stage‐Specific Pressure Programming Decouples Low‐Pressure Sulfur Reduction From High‐Pressure Interfacial Reconstruction in All‐Solid‐State Lithium–Sulfur Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT The commercialization of all‐solid‐state Li–S batteries (ASSLSBs) remains constrained by the “impossible trinity” between high energy density, long cycle life, and low stack pressure. Here we show that stack pressure is not merely a static mechanical boundary, but a stage‐specific regulator of sulfur conversion and interfacial reconstruction. Using a static pressure‐resistance‐overpotential (P‐R‐η) operational threshold algorithm, low‐stack‐pressure operation is predicted feasible for 50 wt% S cathodes. Further operando electrochemical measurements and multiscale chemical and structural characterizations reveal that 1 MPa discharge promotes Li 2 S 2 ‐rich interfacial intermediates. However, constant low‐pressure cycling induces progressive pore filling that prolongs charge transport pathways, leading to inactive Li X S accumulation and triphase interfacial contact losses. State‐resolved very‐small‐angle neutron scattering (VSANS) further uncovers a ∼5 nm structural feature that persists after low‐stack‐pressure discharge, which specifically diminishes upon high‐pressure charging. Guided by this mechanism, we implement a pressure‐programmed protocol combining 1 MPa discharge with 180 MPa charge. The resulting cell retains 98.8% of capacity after 100 cycles at 30 °C. This work establishes a dynamic pressure modulation strategy towards alleviating the “impossible trinity” by decoupling the asymmetric pressure‐electrochemical behaviors.

title: Metallurgical Interface Engineering Constructing In Situ Li 3 N‐Enriched Interphase: A Bulk‐Interface Synergy Strategy Toward Practical Silicon Anodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Silicon anodes are promising for next‐generation lithium‐ion batteries but suffer from volume expansion, unstable solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), and sluggish Li + diffusion. Herein, we report a vacuum‐suspension‐melted (VSM) bulk multiphase integration and interphase modification strategy to address these challenges. Unlike conventional mechanical mixing, VSM constructs a SiSnM (M = Bi, Ni) composite with metallurgically bonded Si/metal interfaces, forming a conductive network that buffers internal stress via atomic‐scale interfacial stress transfer. Simultaneously, a polydopamine‐derived nitrogen‐doped carbon coating transforms in situ into a Li 3 N‐enriched interphase during cycling, which exhibits high ionic/electronic conductivity, accelerates interfacial charge transfer, and suppresses continuous SEI breakdown. The resulting SiSnM@Li 3 N anode delivers 87.3% capacity retention after 1000 cycles at 1.5 A g −1 and >1000 mAh g −1 at 15 A g −1 , with reliable operation from −30°C to 60°C. Stable cycling at 2.5 mg cm −2 confirms practical relevance. Full cells with Li‐rich Mn‐based cathodes show stable performance, and 5 Ah‐level pouch cells deliver 84.7% capacity retention after 300 cycles at 6 A discharge. This work concurrently tackles ionic, electronic, and mechanical constraints, offering a practical path to high‐energy durable Si‐based batteries.

title: Ultra‐Strong, Leak‐Proof Bio‐Based Polyurethane Ionic Fibers for Sustainable Smart Wearables
abstract: ABSTRACT Artificial intelligence (AI)‐integrated digital flexible devices have been widely used in motion detection. However, the emphasis on sensitivity and response speed often overlooks environmental sustainability. Based on a green‐mechanical‐electrical synergistic design, a polar coordination and chemical confinement strategy is proposed to fabricate an ion‐conductive polyurethane fiber. Specifically, chemical confinement refers to the covalent incorporation of the polymerizable ionic‐liquid component into the polyurethane backbone through its hydroxyl‐functionalized imidazolium moiety. Polar coordination involves reversible Mg 2+ –carbonyl interactions that contribute to mechanical reinforcement and Mg 2+ retention. The resulting fiber exhibits a tensile strength of 52.75 MPa and an elongation at break of 1414%. Meanwhile, the in situ grafted ionic liquid provides an ionic conductivity of 0.209 mS cm −1 . After 120 h of vigorous stirring in water, the Mg concentration in the test medium reached 1.9 ppm, showing limited Mg release under the tested condition. Integrating this fiber into smart fabrics enables full‐body motion monitoring and accurate recognition of complex movements with 100% accuracy. This study establishes a closed‐loop paradigm from sustainable molecular design to AI‐driven decision‐making, offering new material design insights for next‐generation green, safe, and high‐performance smart wearable devices.

title: Topological‐Insulator‐Based Ion‐Electron‐Coupled Nanochannels With a Photothermally Induced Thermoelectric Field for Enhanced Ionic Transport
abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient ion transport is essential for high‐performance energy storage and conversion, yet strong ion–channel interactions in conventional highly polar nanochannels can increase migration barriers and impede rapid ion motion. Here, we report layered ion‐electron‐coupled Bi 2 Te 3 /Ti 3 C 2 T x nanochannels, in which ion transport is synergistically regulated by highly polar interfaces, highly conductive surface states, and a photothermally induced thermoelectric field. The polar MXene interfaces support selective ion transport, whereas the highly conductive surface states of Bi 2 Te 3 enhance interfacial electronic responsiveness, facilitating charge equilibration and mitigating local charge accumulation during ion migration. This interfacial coupling reduces the ion‐transport activation energy to 8.02 kJ mol −1 , 34.6% lower than that of pristine MXene nanochannels. As a functional demonstration of enhanced ion transport, the nanochannels deliver a 5.56‐fold increase in osmotic power density (18.9 W m −2 ) under a 50‐fold NaCl concentration gradient. Upon illumination, the photothermally induced temperature gradient activates the Seebeck response of Bi 2 Te 3 , providing an additional thermoelectric driving force for directional ion migration, as reflected by a further increase in power density to 25.5 W m −2 . This work provides a strategy for enhancing ion transport under nanoconfinement through interfacial‐electronic‐coupling‐mediated regulation and thermoelectric‐field‐assisted driving.

title: π‑Conjugated Helical Polymer for Circularly Polarized Photodetection and Secure Optoelectronic Encoding
abstract: ABSTRACT Helical polymers are promising materials for circularly polarized light (CPL) detection and hardware‐level information security owing to their tunable chiroptical properties, efficient charge transport, and intrinsic conformational randomness. However, designing helical polymers with high chiroptical activity, which can be effectively translated intohigh‐performance CPL detection remains challenging. Herein, we reported the helical polymer, ( SSSS )‐diPDI‐C8‐T‐T, in which point chirality was effectively transferred to π‐extended diperylene diimide (diPDI) backbone. Compared with non‐helical polymer ( SS )‐PDI‐C8‐T‐T, ( SSSS )‐diPDI‐C8‐T‐T exhibited chiroptical activity (the absorption dissymmetry factors, g abs = −1.4 × 10 −3 at 460 nm) in chloroform (10 −5 M), owing to the optimized electric–magnetic ( µ ‐ m ) transition dipole alignment. CPL detectors based on ( SSSS )‐diPDI‐C8‐T‐T annealed thin films exhibited higher average photocurrent dissymmetry factors ( g ph ) of 0.52 at 535 nm and −1.03 at 405 nm, the latter of which is the highest g ph reported for single‐component chiral polymer‐based CPL detection. The enhanced chirality‐induced spin selectivity (CISS) effect increased the spin polarization to 89.03%, contributing to the higher g ph for ( SSSS )‐diPDI‐C8‐T‐T annealed thin films. Leveraging the dual‐wavelength CPL response of ( SSSS )‐diPDI‐C8‐T‐T annealed thin films and spatial randomness, 5 × 8 CPL‐PUF array enabled optoelectronic fingerprinting, with inter‐ and intra‐Hamming distances of 49.278% and 1.655%, respectively. This work highlights helical polymers for CPL detection and chiral optoelectronic fingerprinting.

title: One-Dimensional Organic Polynanomers: Design, Synthesis, Properties, and Applications
abstract: Conspectus π-Conjugated polymers (π-CPs) have emerged as promising candidates for next-generation semiconductors, following four generations of inorganic semiconductors and driven by rapid advances in flexible electronics. Since the discovery of conducting polymers in 1977, they have become foundational active materials for plastic electronics, enabling applications in light-emitting diodes, lasers, solar cells, and transistor circuits for sensing, computing, and actuation. However, polymer light-emitting diodes (PLEDs) have not been commercialized, whereas organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) based on molecular emitters have captured a substantial market share. Moreover, organic polymer solar cells face intense competition from perovskite solar cells, while polymer-based systems for perception, memory and computing, actuation, and telecommunication remain largely at the fundamental research stage. The convergence of organic chemistry, polymer chemistry, supramolecular chemistry, and colloid chemistry has established organic nanoscience and technology as a unified frontier, providing robust methodologies to overcome existing limitations in reshaping π-conjugated polymers and improving their device functionality and performance. In this context, we have developed a revolutionary strategy of gridization and polygridization of organic compounds, a covalent assembly approach that transforms discrete conjugated nanoatoms and nanomolecules into soluble organic nanopolymers (also termed polynanomers). These nanomaterials exhibit one-dimensional chain architectures at the nanoscale with high length-to-width ratios, as first reported in 2017 for organic nanopolymers based on organic nanogrids. This Account summarizes our systematic progress from cross-scale molecular design to device applications, covering nanostructure design, nanosynthesis, characterization, aggregate-phase morphology, unique optoelectronic and mechanical properties, and potential applications in organic devices. We designed and synthesized a series of organic nanopolymers (ONP1-ONP12), classified into three categories: π-interrupted and nonconjugated polynanomers, fully conjugated polynanomers, and polyspironanomers. Key breakthroughs include the discovery of drawing-hand grid (DHGs, ONP2) with exclusive meso-stereoselectivity, double-stranded nanopolyspirogrids (NPSGs, ONP12) with ultrahigh persistence length, and A-type single-atom catalysts (ONP10 and ONP11) that enable CO2-to-methanol conversion with near-unity selectivity. Conventional polymers typically adopt a coil conformation, whereas organic nanopolymers enhance main-chain anisotropy through the volume repulsion effect of nanoreplicating units, thereby increasing the rheological-optical coefficients. Concurrently, a stronger volume repulsion effect can inhibit conformational relaxation of the main chain and significantly enhance framework rigidity, thereby weakening the nonradiative transition behavior of excitons. Finally, we provide a perspective on the precise construction of organic cross-scale materials featuring interconvertible nanoarchitectures spanning zero to three dimensions, programmable nanostructures, persistent morphologies, and predictable optoelectronic properties across dimensions and length scales. Soluble organic nanopolymers are expected to become the next-generation macromolecular materials beyond engineering plastics, enabling flexible electronics and mechatronics for embedded intelligence and artificial chemists in the forthcoming era of consciousness.

title: Stress-adaptive manufacturing of a cellulose nanofiber/carbon nanotube-liquid metal dual-functional layer for dendrite-free zinc metal deposition
abstract: Abstract Zn plating/stripping continuously reconstructs the anode interface, where uncontrolled metal growth induces current-field distortion, Zn 2+ flux heterogeneity, and stress accumulation, ultimately causing dendrite growth, hydrogen evolution, corrosion, and byproduct accumulation. Herein, a manufacturable cellulose nanofiber/carbon nanotube (CNF/CNT)-GaInZn hybrid interface (CC/GaInZn) anode is reported that couples a flexible conductive fibrous scaffold with a deformable solid‒liquid biphasic interface to regulate zinc deposition across electrical, mechanical, and chemical dimensions. CNF/CNT provides a uniform local reaction environment and current distribution, which results in uniform zinc deposition. GaInZn layer reduces the nucleation barrier, suppresses the hydrogen evolution reaction, and dissipates the deposition stress. As a result, the CC/GaInZn symmetric battery operates stably for over 4 200 h at 0.5 mA·cm −2 and 0.5 mAh·cm −2 with low polarization. COMSOL simulations reveal that the CC/GaInZn layer effectively homogenizes Zn 2+ distribution, thereby enabling uniform zinc nucleation and growth. Notably, XRD residual stress analysis reveals a transition from high tensile stress to compressive stress in Zn deposits on CC/GaInZn, providing direct evidence for interfacial stress release and dendrite-suppressed Zn plating. This work demonstrates a strategy for constructing adaptive functional metal interfaces for aqueous zinc energy storage devices.

title: Surface Termination Controls Symmetric Block Copolymer Transport through Nanopores
abstract: Abstract Understanding how polymer architecture governs transport through nanopores is essential for nanocomposite fabrication, membrane design, and functional coatings. However, the effect of the nanoscale structure of copolymers on chain transport through nanoporous media remains poorly understood. In this study, we demonstrate that simply inverting the surface orientation of lamellar poly(styrene-block-2-vinylpyridine) (PS-b-P2VP) diblock copolymers, composed of two monomers with strongly contrasting affinities for SiO2, at the entrance of a nanoporous packing of SiO2 nanoparticles significantly alters the kinetics of capillary rise infiltration (CaRI). Using in situ spectroscopic ellipsometry, we find that infiltration of the PS-b-P2VP symmetric diblock copolymer into SiO2 nanoparticle (NP) packings is significantly faster when the P2VP domain is the top layer of the block copolymer film and is therefore the first to contact the NPs, compared to when the PS domain is the top layer. Coarse-grained molecular dynamics (CGMD) simulations reveal that this difference originates from block-specific adsorption pathways that reorganize the nanophase structure around NPs: P2VP-first infiltration forms thin adsorbed layers that drive PS into the pore interiors, producing larger PS-rich regions with greater apparent connectivity, which is associated with a higher upward chain flux. In contrast, PS-first infiltration produces thicker P2VP layers that result in smaller, more fragmented PS-rich regions and a lower upward chain flux. Above the order–disorder transition (ODT), or upon silanizing NPs to neutralize surface affinity, the rate difference disappears. These findings demonstrate how the interplay between nanoscale domain configuration and polymer–surface affinity governs infiltration dynamics, providing mechanistic insight into controlling transport in nanostructured block copolymers and into designing high-loading composites, selective membranes, and functional coatings with controlled transport pathways.

title: Solvothermal Domino Synthesis of a Cu(I) Bis‐imidazo[1,5‐ a ]pyridine Complex: Reaction Process Tracking and Potent Antitumor Activity
abstract: Although numerous metal complexes exhibit promising antitumor efficacy, their synthesis still relies on inefficient stepwise routes that require separate organic ligand preparation followed by metal coordination. title: Inorganic Ionic Polymerization toward Fracture-Resistant, Self-healable Functional Hydrogels
abstract: Abstract Fracture-resistant, self-healable functional hydrogels hold promise for soft robotics, wearable electronics, and intelligent devices. However, integrating these properties within a single structure remains challenging. Persistent load-bearing constraints hinder molecular rearrangement for repair, whereas excessive network dynamics can disrupt functional organization. Here, we uncover a reciprocal assembly mechanism based on bidirectional regulation between inorganic ionic oligomers and polymer chains. The acrylic acid/poly(acrylic acid) (PAA) environment suppresses calcium carbonate oligomer (CCO) aggregation, while CCO organizes PAA chains into birefringent acicular domains through multisite coordination and cooperative hydrogen bonding. These domains provide persistent load-bearing constraints and exchangeable interactions, enabling a fracture energy of 38.3 kJ m–2 and 87% tensile-strength recovery after 6 h of ambient healing. The same assembled network further exhibits 4.5% AM1.5G solar-weighted absorptivity and strong mid-infrared emission, remaining 5.1 °C cooler than neat PAA under simulated sunlight while retaining its cooling response for 21 days. This work establishes inorganic ionic oligomers as active reciprocal regulators of polymer organization, coupling dynamic network reconstruction with mechanical reinforcement and functional stability.

title: Direct Inkjet Printing of Covalent Organic Frameworks
abstract: Abstract There is a growing need for gas and volatile organic compound (VOC) sensors in many areas, including air quality, safety monitoring, and (early) disease detection. VOC sensors can make use of affinity coatings to increase their sensitivity and selectivity. With their intrinsic high surface areas and chemically tunable pores, covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are excellent candidates for the design and fabrication of such affinity coatings. However, precise, scalable, and easy deposition of such COF materials is proven to still be a challenge. In this study, we show the controlled deposition of COFs through direct inkjet printing for the first time, for which COFs are prepared as colloidal suspensions, serving as ready-to-use inks. We present a facile colloidal synthesis, leading to colloidal suspensions that are stable for months and which allow inkjet printing without any further processing. The COFs can be printed on gold as both isolated spots and as thin layers. The synthesis and printing conditions were carefully optimized to strike the balance between colloidal stability, printing robustness, and controlled drying. After exposure to saturated VOC environments, the printed layers show VOC desorption as monitored by infrared reflection absorption spectroscopy, not only confirming partial retention of the porous nature of the printed COF particles but also demonstrating the applicability of printed COF layers as affinity coatings on VOC sensors.

title: Solvent-Mediated Self-Assembly of Sulfomethylated Lignin into Nanoparticles: Linking Molecular Interactions, Internal Organization, and Interfacial Function
abstract: Abstract Lignin nanoparticles (LNPs) are increasingly explored as sustainable colloidal materials, yet the molecular factors governing their self-assembly and interfacial behavior remain poorly understood. Here, the effects of lignin chemistry, solvent quality, and lignin concentration on nanoparticle formation were systematically investigated using kraft lignin (KL) and sulfomethylated lignin (SL). Hansen solubility parameter analysis demonstrated that solvent−lignin affinity governed supersaturation and nucleation during solvent exchange. Sulfomethylation produced nanoparticles with a significantly smaller hydrodynamic diameter and narrower size distribution than kraft lignin nanoparticles. 1H NMR analysis revealed a distinct internal organization in SL nanoparticles, characterized by hydrophilic groups enriched within the particle core and hydrophobic groups concentrated in the shell. In oil−water emulsions, SL nanoparticles formed dense interfacial layers and reduced the average droplet size. These findings establish how lignin functionalization and solvent-mediated self-assembly collectively govern nanoparticle structure and interfacial performance, providing mechanistic guidelines for the design of lignin-based colloidal materials.

title: Tunable microscale assembly with ultrasound vortex tweezers
abstract: Abstract Ultrasound tweezers provide a powerful approach for the contactless manipulation of microscale objects, yet achieving structurally simple platforms capable of tunable particle assembly remains challenging. Here, we introduce ultrasound vortex tweezers based on a Fresnel-spiral diffraction grating (FSDG) that converts an incident ultrasonic plane wave into a vortex beam carrying orbital angular momentum. The passive grating structure enables the generation of ultrasound vortex fields with tunable topological charge, producing ring-shaped trapping regions with adjustable spatial scales. Using this platform, we demonstrate the controllable self-rotation of individual microparticles, tunable aggregation of multiple particles, and core-shell encapsulation in bidisperse particle systems. The rotational speed of the trapped particles shows an overall increasing trend with increasing vortex order, while the aggregation and encapsulation processes can be regulated through the vortex order, driving voltage, and actuation time. These results establish ultrasound vortex tweezers as a compact and versatile strategy for tunable microscale assembly, offering new opportunities for high-precision ultrasound manipulation in materials engineering and biofabrication.

title: Molecular Mechanism of Salt-Induced Fibrinogen Self-Assembly
abstract: Abstract Fibrinogen nanofiber scaffolds, which closely mimic the fibrous architecture of the extracellular matrix, have emerged as promising biomaterials for wound healing and tissue engineering. Salt-induced, thrombin-free fibrinogen fiber assembly provides a versatile route for their fabrication, yet the molecular mechanism underlying its pronounced ion specificity has remained unresolved. Here, we combined complementary experimental analyses with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to identify the structural determinants governing phosphate-induced fibrillogenesis. MD simulations suggested that phosphate, but not chloride, preferentially stabilizes extended fibrinogen conformations through persistent interactions with the E domain and αC region, thereby increasing αC accessibility. Consistent with this mechanism, four complementary perturbation strategies, αC-domain truncation, antibody-mediated masking of the αC region, competitive inhibition by isolated αC fragments, and rescue experiments combining truncated fibrinogen with cognate αC fragments resulted in the absence of nanofiber assembly. Docking and MD simulations further demonstrated that preservation of the proposed β-hairpin-mediated αC dimer interface alone is insufficient to drive fibrillogenesis, highlighting the requirement for an intact αC region within native fibrinogen. Together, these findings support a mechanistic model for phosphate-induced fibrinogen fiber assembly and demonstrate that phosphate promotes fibrillogenesis through a molecular pathway distinct from thrombin-mediated fibrin polymerization. This mechanistic framework advances the fundamental understanding of fibrinogen self-assembly and provides a rational basis for the design of thrombin-free fibrinogen-based nanofibrous biomaterials.

title: Green Electrochemical Synthesis of Antimicrobial Polyaldehyde Starch
abstract: Abstract Conventional aldehyde-based biocides raise environmental and safety concerns due to their toxicity and persistence in inhibiting microbiologically influenced corrosion (MIC) in numerous industrial applications. The present study introduces a rapid and sustainable method for synthesizing polyaldehyde starch through electrochemistry (PAS-EC) using soluble starch as feedstock in aqueous salt media with iridium–ruthenium electrodes. This approach has the potential to replace toxic oxidants with a safer alternative, while significantly reducing reaction time and enhancing overall process safety. By minimizing hazardous reagents and streamlining operational steps, it can also contribute to improved sustainability. Taken together, these features make electrochemical methods a promising pathway for application in industrial bioprocesses. Under optimized electrochemical conditions (15 mA cm–2, 15% NaCl, and 1 h), PAS-EC was obtained with 65% yield and a degree of oxidation exceeding 63%, surpassing the conventional periodate-oxidized dialdehyde starch (DAS-PO) with 50% yield and a 48% degree of oxidation. FTIR and NMR characterization confirmed the successful formation of aldehydic groups, while thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) revealed a decrease in thermal stability due to the modification in the structure of pure starch. Biocidal efficacy was assessed against six hydrocarbon-degrading bacterial strains that are extremely relevant to MIC and bioremediation under oil and gas field conditions. PAS-EC displayed promising and broad-spectrum antibacterial activity, with a maximum of 60% inhibition efficiency at 1000 ppm in comparison to glutaraldehyde. Overall, both PAS-EC and DAS-PO demonstrated promising biocidal performance, underscoring their potential as safer and more sustainable alternatives.

title: End-Group Functionalization Reshapes the Self-Assembly and Phase Behavior of Pluronic F68 in Water
abstract: Abstract Pluronic triblock copolymers based on poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO) and poly(propylene oxide) (PPO), with a PEO–PPO–PEO architecture, exhibit thermoresponsive self-assembly governed by the interplay among polymer hydration, micellization, and intermicellar organization. Here, we investigate how terminal bisurethane-methacrylate functionalization affects the aqueous self-assembly and phase behavior of Pluronic F68. The resulting derivative, termed F68-XL, was examined over broad concentration and temperature ranges using differential scanning calorimetry, rheology, small-angle X-ray scattering, and refractive-index measurements. End-group functionalization produces only modest changes in the micellization boundary but markedly alters the conditions under which higher-order micellar organization develops. Compared with pristine F68, F68-XL displays a displacement of the body-centered cubic ordered region toward higher temperatures and polymer concentrations, together with an unusual re-entrant liquid-like–solid-like–liquid-like rheological response at high concentrations. These findings indicate that terminal functionalization affects higher-order organization more strongly than primary micellization and highlight the sensitivity of intermicellar packing and phase stability to Pluronic chain-end chemistry. The photoreactive terminal groups additionally enable UV-induced covalent network formation, establishing the photo-cross-linking capability of F68-XL. Overall, this work identifies end-group functionalization as an effective strategy for modulating the thermoresponsive self-assembly and phase behavior of Pluronic F68 while introducing an additional route to covalent network formation.

title: On the formation of lipid nanoparticles and encapsulation of RNA: kinetics, dynamics, and self-assembly regimes
abstract: RNA-containing lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) form through self-assembly triggered by micromixing of an organic lipid solution against an aqueous antisolvent, leading to supersaturation and consequent nanoprecipitation. The kinetics of this process remain poorly understood. Here, we employ millisecond-resolved flowthrough small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) coupled to a multi-inlet vortex mixer (MIVM), confined impinging jets mixer (CIJM) and a T-junction mixer, to experimentally investigate the earliest stages of LNP self-assembly. Ordered LNPs show a characteristic high-q feature indicative of the ionizable lipid-RNA complex; changes in the evolution, shape, and intensity of this peak and the overall particle size in the low-q feature reveal changes in particle assembly and RNA cargo encapsulation. Results captured within milliseconds of mixing show that under turbulent flow (water/ethanol ratio 3:1), LNPs are fully formed by as early as 12 ms, including liquid-crystalline internal organization that indicates RNA encapsulation. Adjusting the water/ethanol ratio to 1:1 results in LNPs with a less ordered nanostructure, in line with reports that downstream processing plays a major role in the final structure of particles formed under these solvent conditions. These findings shed light on the mechanisms by which mixing conditions influence LNP formation. We propose a framework of four distinct self-assembly pathways defined by mixing time (i.e. faster or slower than the O(10ms) self-assembly time) and loading strategy (i.e. RNA introduced during the LNP self-assembly step, or in a second step). This provides a basis for understanding how mixing and loading strategies govern LNP formation and homogeneous RNA encapsulation, particularly for high molecular weight RNA payloads. The results establish process-structure-function relationships that support rational optimization for LNP manufacturing processes.

title: Multiscale Modelling of Energy Materials
abstract: The conflicts between accuracy and efficiency of simulation have significantly limited the precision and scope of modelling in materials science. By integrating different computational techniques across various scales, it is possible to achieve a balance that enhances both precision and scope. This PhD thesis focuses on the multiscale modeling of energy materials, demonstrating the power and effectiveness of multiscale simulation in understanding and predicting material properties. The study covers a broad spectrum of materials and methodologies as given in graphical abstract, including density functional theory calculation (DFT) of organic-inorganic hybrid perovskites, molecular dynamics simulation of carbon-supported metal Ru nanoparticles, and the Monte-Carlo simulation of self-assembly of flurbiprofen molecules on metal surfaces. At the quantum scale, DFT calculations are employed to investigate the stability and electronic structure of halogen molecules intercalation in layered hybrid perovskites. For example, the manipulation of the bandgap and charge carrier mobility of layered perovskites through intercalation is explored, highlighting the impact of halogen bonding on the properties of such family of materials. At the atomic scale, Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations provide a detailed understanding of the morphology and stability of carbon-supported Ru nanoparticles. The simulations reveal how metal support interactions and metal structural arrangements influence the stability of these nanoparticles. At the mesoscale, Monte Carlo (MC) simulations capture the self-assembly behavior of flurbiprofen on metal surfaces. The simulations show how molecule-molecule interactions drive the formation of ordered nanostructures, offering insights into the design of materials with specific chiral properties. Overall, this thesis highlights the critical role of multiscale modeling in advancing the field of energy materials, offering a detailed understanding of material behavior across different scales.

title: An Integrated Coarse-Grained Simulation and Graph-Transformer Framework for the Discovery of Self-Assembling Cyclic Peptides
abstract: Abstract Self-assembling cyclic peptides are promising building blocks for functional biomaterials owing to their enhanced structural stability, proteolytic resistance, and diverse supramolecular architectures. However, how cyclization regulates peptide self-assembly remains poorly understood, and computational frameworks specifically developed for cyclic peptides are still lacking. Here, we demonstrate that disulfide-mediated cyclization fundamentally reshapes peptide self-assembly by significantly enhancing aggregation propensity (AP) and promoting the formation of diverse nanostructures compared with their linear counterparts, as confirmed by coarse-grained molecular dynamics (CGMD) simulations and experimental characterization. Motivated by these findings, we established an integrated computational-experimental framework for the prediction and rational design of self-assembling disulfide-cyclized peptides. A data set comprising 8,000 cyclic pentapeptides was generated using CGMD simulations, and multiple machine learning and deep learning models were systematically evaluated, among which a Graph-Transformer achieved the best predictive performance (R2 = 0.971). The optimized model was subsequently applied to high-throughput screening of 160,000 cyclic hexapeptides using a ranking strategy integrating AP and hydrophobicity, leading to the identification of multiple previously unreported self-assembling candidates. Experimental validation showed excellent agreement with model predictions. Furthermore, systematic sequence analysis revealed residue- and position-dependent assembly rules unique to disulfide-cyclized peptide systems. This work establishes a computational framework for the rapid discovery of self-assembling disulfide-cyclized peptides and provides new mechanistic insights and design principles for peptide-based functional materials.

title: Meso–microporous zeolitic materials with thin walls containing ordered 10-ring channels
abstract: Aluminosilicate zeolites offer exceptional size and shape selectivity but suffer from diffusion limitations imposed by subnanometer micropores. Intrinsically meso–microporous zeolites integrate mesopores with micropores to create interconnected pathways that accelerate diffusion while preserving selectivity, yet their synthesis remains challenging. In this study, we report NJU120-5 and NJU120-7, intrinsically meso–microporous aluminosilicates that integrate micropores with mesopores enclosed by two-T-atom-thick walls containing 10-ring channels, forming a fully interconnected three-dimensional pore network. Their plausible framework models were established on the basis of advanced electron ptychographic imaging, revealing representative quasi-rectangular mesopores in calcined NJU120-5 with a uniform width of ~12 angstroms and lengths from 41 to 162 angstroms. Both materials exhibit high porosity, strong Brønsted acidity, and enhanced performance in heavy-oil cracking, delivering high yields of valuable fuels with suppressed coke formation.
